reason: Full-batch review found significant physical-prerequisite and scope gaps requiring owner resolution.

findings.reason: The incompressible Newtonian clause requires eta>0 and the barotropic inviscid clause does not supply constant-density incompressible Euler, yet pthm-cm17-incompressible-periodic-local-evolution uses nu=0 and ex-cm17-periodic-shear-exact-solution-check claims that branch; add the missing adopted assumption.

The definition says fields transfer by composition, while the kinematic postulate requires Galilean covariance but defines only velocity and acceleration transforms; scalar, vector, tensor and reference-label rules for rho, b, t, sigma, p and xi are missing for the mass, momentum, elastic and fluid laws.

The normalized unit-torus theorem is applied with dimensionful nu=eta/rho, velocity u and an H^s-based time T without spatial, velocity or time scales; pthm-cm17-incompressible-periodic-local-evolution and ex-cm17-periodic-shear-exact-solution-check need a stated nondimensionalization and physical-time conversion.

Clause (ii) admits every piecewise-C1 D whose closure lies in the field domain, which may extend beyond Omega_s, while the stated physical scope restricts balances to regions inside the body; make D subset Omega_s explicit for pthm-cm17-stress-matrix-and-symmetry and pthm-cm17-momentum-equation.

Clause (iii) says contact force equals integral(rho b-rho a), but its displayed balance and the supplier's t(n)=sigma n convention imply contact plus body force equals inertia; align the reading without changing the consistent equation.

physical_scope claims equivalence of force-form balance and the local momentum equation, but the Statement and Proof establish only the forward implication; preserve the claim by proving the converse from the existing regularity and divergence theorem.

The density is defined only on U containing the swept set over a compactly contained J0, but m(t,B') is defined for every t in I where rho may be undefined; restrict m to covered times or require U to contain the full swept interval.

Clause (iii) uses unquantified B in ||v0||<=B and says the second solution has v(0)=u(0) rather than v(0)=v0; define B and the common time T_B and state the two initial-data assignments to match the cited stability theorem.

Clause (b) integrates a pressure law from 1 to a dimensionful density without a reference-density or normalization convention; define a positive reference density or explicitly nondimensionalize the density variable.

The expansion uses 1+t although t has seconds under the framework units; specify a rate alpha with dimension inverse-time in chi and carry it through the interval, density and derivative calculations.

The final remark says W vanishes exactly on rigid translations, but the supplier proves W(e)=0 iff e=0 and infinitesimal rigid rotations also have zero linear strain; qualify the field-level characterization.
